item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine launched drones that struck Russia's largest oil refinery in Siberia, while Russian forces killed a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker in a drone strike and downed a Ukrainian drone in Russia's Smolensk region, killing two people. Russia reported intercepting 146 drones in the Leningrad region and a drone that wounded three energy workers in Sumy Oblast. A U.S.-mediated prisoner swap was concluded in Abu Dhabi, but broader peace talks ended without a breakthrough. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israel struck Gaza’s Nasser Hospital, killing six people including a doctor, a child and a senior Hamas commander inside the facility. Heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents, threatening power and healthcare access and leaving families exposed to cold, with a baby reported to have died from the temperature. Humanitarians have called for swift entry of winter supplies into Gaza as the humanitarian situation worsens due to disputes between Israel and Hamas. The United Nations reported 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Israel has intensified its operations in southern Lebanon, striking Qantara, conducting overflights that wounded a Lebanese footballer, and detonating a large explosion in Khiam while drones flew over Beirut. The Lebanese army seized a large quantity of weapons in a Beirut suburb warehouse and reported another arms depot capture in the city’s southern suburbs. Hezbollah arrested five members in Batroun, continued artillery fire on Israeli positions, and began cash payments to war victims and displaced families. UNRWA funding cuts have deepened hardship for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
The Houthis have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, striking a pumping station and the East-West oil pipeline, while Saudi forces report intercepting missiles and drones with debris falling near Mecca, which the Houthis deny targeting. Syria is weighing sending troops to aid Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis, and France is favouring added pressure on the Houthis, according to their foreign ministry spokesperson. Pakistan has called for an immediate end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as the UN Security Council renews Yemen sanctions, and the Houthis held a mass funeral while urging actions to protect civilians. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

In eastern Deir ez-Zor, unidentified gunmen killed one Syrian soldier and wounded two others, and similar attacks were reported in Jadidat Bakara. Lebanon has asked Syria to extradite suspects linked to the killing of an ex-Iraqi MP. Syrian security officials are restructuring the army and preparing new security and administrative changes. item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iran-backed suspects are accused of plotting attacks on a U.K. air base that hosts U.S. jets in Iraq. A separate Iran-backed trio is linked to a drone strike on the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan that halted production and cut power. Iraqi security officials announced expanded air defence deployments, the formation of a special security force and an energy police unit to combat oil smuggling and protect pipelines, and they are sending a delegation to Lebanon to assist the inquiry into former MP Ahmed al-Alwani’s death. 396 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army has seized the towns of Bakori and Sali in West Kordofan while the Rapid Support Forces continue drone strikes that have killed civilians in the Blue Nile and White Nile, including a strike that killed nine civilians in the Blue Nile. Drones now account for two thirds of child casualties in the conflict and a senior RSF commander defected to the army after 13 years of service. Vinícius Jr of Real Madrid sent a surprise video message to a Sudanese boy who received prosthetic legs after a drone strike. There were 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
UN peacekeepers are accused of failing to protect civilians before the Abiemnom massacre that killed at least 213 people, and Amnesty International is calling for investigations into the authorities and UN. Clashes continue between government forces and opposition fighters in Akobo while governors in Jonglei and Aweil East urge peace ahead of elections scheduled for next month, which envoys warn could unravel fragile stability. A convoy ambush in South Sudan killed two people, including a journalist, and a CityLink Aviation plane crashed near Juba killing all 14 aboard. The humanitarian situation deepens with hunger, displacement and ongoing sexual violence, and 2 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Federal forces have seized additional Tigray cities while fighting continues, and severe drought and prolonged conflict are driving acute hunger in Amhara, Tigray and Afar. Ethiopian drones are now operating over Sudan and RSF drones are launching from Ethiopian territory against Sudanese targets, prompting diplomatic expulsions and consular closures. An RPG strike near a school in Moyale killed dozens of Ethiopian Orthodox believers and a Kenyan, and attacks on Orthodox Christians persist in Arsi, Benishangul Gumuz and the north, with blasts heard in Addis Ababa. Seed insecurity threatens Tigray farmers and a psychosocial and spiritual care pilot is being tested, while displacement exceeds 50,000 people, and 2,824 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ukrainian officers are training Sahel militants on drone use, adding a new external dimension to the conflict. In northern Nigeria, violence forced tens of thousands of civilians to flee into Niger, and opposition leader Atiku accused President Tinubu of failing Nigerians after 638 people were killed and 64,000 fled.
